title: Take a sorted sample
summary: ORDER BY arranges rows before LIMIT chooses a few.
introduction: ORDER BY arranges rows before LIMIT chooses a few. Your task: Change the ordering to longest books first.
learningObjectives: Change the ordering to longest books first.
Explain the example for take a sorted sample

blocks.text: ORDER BY arranges rows before LIMIT chooses a few. This makes a shortest-book query clear.

Use MariaDB 10.11+ with its mariadb client in an empty practice database. These dialect-specific examples do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Keep the sample database separate from real records.

blocks.code: SELECT title,pages FROM cma_maria_books ORDER BY pages,title LIMIT 3;
blocks.title: Take a sorted sample

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The query returns at most three rows with the smallest page counts first.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A LIMIT without an order does not promise which rows appear first.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change the ordering to longest books first.
